 Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Bryce Hopkins, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Jokić will start Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 The Nuggets are down two rotation wings for Saturday’s game, as Cameron Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (wrist) will not play. Hopkins gets the starting nod, keeping DeMar DeRozan in the sixth-man role. The other four starters are unchanged. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Denver Nuggets

 Alpha Diallo 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #11

 Alpha Diallo (wrist) is out for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Diallo’s absence means that the Nuggets will be without two rotation players, as starter Cameron Johnson (ankle) was already out. DeMar DeRozan could move into the starting lineup after coming off the bench in Denver’s season-opening loss to the Thunder. 
 Alpha Diallo 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #11 
 Alpha Diallo (wrist) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Pelicans. 
 Diallo played 22 minutes in his Nuggets’ debut on Thursday, starting the second half for the injured Cameron Johnson (ankle). With Johnson ruled out for Saturday, Diallo could start Denver’s home opener if he’s available. If not, DeMar DeRozan may start. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 DEN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 DeMar DeRozan produced 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs) and two rebounds in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 DeRozan was used in a reserve role on Thursday, and that’s likely how he’ll be used on nights when the Nuggets are healthy. More importantly, he got 28 minutes in his Nuggets debut. DeRozan’s issues on Thursday: foul shooting and turnovers. In addition to missing three of six from the charity stripe, DeRozan recorded five turnovers. He’s averaged more than 2.5 turnovers per game once in his NBA career, so fantasy managers shouldn’t worry about Thursday’s number. 
 Cameron Johnson 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Cameron Johnson (ankle) is questionable to return to Thursday’s game against the Thunder. 
 Johnson injured his right ankle during the first half of Thursday’s season opener and did not start the third quarter. Alpha Diallo started the period in Johnson’s place. If Johnson doesn’t return, Diallo and DeMar DeRozan stand to gain the most in playing time. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 DEN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 DeMar DeRozan accounted for 14 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), one rebound, five assists, one steal and two blocks in Friday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 After sitting out Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers, DeRozan played 27 minutes off the bench on Friday. He’ll be asked to do what he’s done throughout his career: score, albeit in a reserve role. With Julian Strawther (knee) out for at least six weeks, DeRozan’s scoring ability becomes even more important. While this may lower DeRozan’s fantasy ceiling, he remains a solid option for fantasy managers punting three-pointers. 
 Julian Strawther 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Julian Strawther (knee) finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Clippers with 11 points (4-of-9 FGs), two rebounds and three three-pointers. 
 Strawther was injured in the third quarter of Wednesday’s game when he fell awkwardly, landing with his left leg beneath him after being trapped by two Clippers defenders. Following the game, Nuggets head coach David Adelman said that Strawther will undergo an MRI on Thursday. If he misses time, the Nuggets will rely even more on DeMar DeRozan (who did not play on Wednesday) off the bench. 
 Bryce Hopkins 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 Nuggets signed Bryce Hopkins to a two-way contract. 
 The 49th overall pick in the 2026 draft, Hopkins had a productive Summer League run in Las Vegas. The former St. John’s standout has been rewarded with a two-way deal, and there could be times during the season when he’s called upon to provide added depth on the wing. While worthy of a look in dynasty leagues, there’s no need to consider Hopkins in redraft formats during draft season. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 DEN 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 NBA insider Chris Haynes reports DeMar DeRozan intends to sign with the Nuggets. 
 DeRozan was waived by the Kings in early July, and he has now found a new home for his 18th NBA season. He spent the last two in Sacramento and will remain in the West, though on a more competitive team. DeRozan will have a chance to start, but it is more likely that he is used in a reserve capacity. DeRozan has only come off the bench 12 times in his career, all during his rookie season. He’ll likely take another hit in production due to a minutes decrease next season. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 FA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 NBA insider Marc Stein reports that the Trail Blazers are not pursuing free agent DeMar DeRozan. 
 DeRozan’s time with the Kings ended earlier this summer, and there has been speculation about his next stop. Miami, Denver, Cleveland and Washington have reportedly expressed interest in the veteran wing, and there were also reports that Portland was involved. However, according to Stein, the Trail Blazers have not pursued the possibility of signing DeRozan. Given the team’s surplus of perimeter players, it is unsurprising that Portland would not be in the mix for the 36-year-old. 
 DeMar DeRozan 
 FA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #10 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Wizards have been in contact with free agent DeMar DeRozan recently. 
 In the aftermath of his exit from Sacramento, DeRozan was considered to be a player likely headed to a team with postseason ambitions. Miami, Cleveland and Denver have all expressed interest since the veteran wing hit free agency, and now Washington has reportedly worked its way into the mix. Given the number of young wings on the Wizards’ roster, adding DeRozan would create even more of a logjam, potentially limiting the short-term fantasy potential of a Kyshawn George or Will Riley.

 Trevon Brazile provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (6-of-101FGs), nine rebounds, one steal, two blocks and three three-pointers against the Pelicans on Saturday.
 With Cameron Johnson (ankle) sidelined, Bryce Hopkins got the starting nod in his place. However, he only played 19 minutes to Brazile’s 28, which led all reserves. Brazile wasn’t able to get much offense going in his debut, but he was able to knock down some big shots in this game, which included seven of Denver’s 15 points in overtime. The second-round pick is quickly looking like one of the better value picks from the summer, and he should be an important piece for Denver this season, though fantasy managers should exercise caution before adding the rookie. This level of production may not continue consistently. However, he absolutely deserves praise for his immediate production.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Jamal Murray 
 DEN 
 Guard 
 #27 
 Player Stats

 Jamal Murray led the Nuggets with 42 points (12-of-25 FGs, 10-of-13 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and eight three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime win over the Pelicans on Saturday.
 After being held to just six points in the season opener, Murray bounced back in a big way in this game. He led Denver in scoring and accounted for over half of their three-pointers. He wasn’t able to get any offense going in overtime, but it was his heroics at the end of the game that forced the extra frame. He’ll look to carry this offensive production into Monday’s matchup with the Warriors, and fantasy managers shouldn’t expect to see many more six-point outings from him.
 -  Noah Rubin 
 Recap

 Nikola Jokić 
 DEN 
 Center 
 #15 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Nikola Jokić stuffed the stat sheet on Saturday with 35 points (12-of-23 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), 15 rebounds, 10 assists, two steals, three blocks, three three-pointers and six turnovers against the Pelicans.
 The first five quarters of Jokić’s season were rough, but he seems to have figured things out. He shot 1-of-5 and turned the ball over three times in the first quarter of this game, but he got back to producing at a high level after that. This was his first triple-double of the season, though he did need the extra five minutes to get there since seven of his boards came during overtime. He’ll continue to produce like a top-three player in fantasy basketball despite struggling in the season opener.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dejounte Murray

 Dejounte Murray posted a full line on Saturday with 22 points (9-of-18 FGs), six rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Nuggets.
 It hasn’t resulted in a win yet, but Murray has been productive to start the season. His minutes are back up after being limited last season, and he’s shooting efficiently, unlike his first year with the Pelicans. Of course, he’s still contributing value across the board, and even with Jeremiah Fears starting, he still has the ball in his hands a ton. He’ll look to keep it going in the rematch with Denver on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Trey Murphy led the Pelicans with 26 points (10-of-16 FGs), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in a 141-135 overtime loss to the Nuggets on Saturday.
 Murphy struggled in the Pelicans’ first two games of the season, but he was able to get back on track in this one. He led New Orleans in scoring and surpassed his total points from the first two games. This type of performance was more in line with what he has been able to produce over the last two seasons, and he’ll look to keep it going in their next game, which will be a rematch with Denver on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Derik Queen

 Derik Queen provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), eight rebounds and two assists against the Nuggets on Saturday.
 With Yves Missi (knee) sidelined for this game, head coach Jamahl Mosley opted to start DeAndre Jordan in his place. Jordan played 20 minutes, while Queen played 24 and was more productive, as expected. The Pelicans don’t play again until Wednesday, which is the first leg of a back-to-back. If Missi remains out, Queen should see a boost, and Jordan still wouldn’t be worth streaming.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Josh Giddey 
 CHI 
 Guard

 Player Stats

 Josh Giddey accounted for nine points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 After shooting a combined 4-of-19 from the field in Chicago’s first two games, Giddey was considerably better on Saturday. Although he finished with just nine points, fantasy managers will be pleased with his rebounds and assists. Over three games, Giddey has shot 26.9 percent from the field and 50.0 percent from the foul line, numbers that must improve if he’s to justify his second-round ADP from the preseason. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Recap

 Norman Powell 
 CHI 
 Guard 
 #24 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Norman Powell produced 18 points (4-of-12 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, four steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Wizards.
 Powell’s offensive role may be slightly larger than he anticipated when he signed with the Bulls, but it raises his fantasy ceiling. However, fantasy managers will reap the rewards only if he improves his accuracy. Through three games, Powell has shot 14-of-41 (34.1%) from the field, nearly 13 percentage points lower than his career number (47.0%). He’ll look to clean that up during the Bulls’ three-game Week 2, which starts on Monday in Boston. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Recap 
 More Norman Powell News
 Matas Buzelis 
 CHI 
 Forward 
 #14 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Matas Buzelis finished Saturday’s loss to the Wizards with 21 points (7-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Buzelis had a difficult start to the season, totaling 24 points on 4-of-17 shooting. A 13-of-16 night at the foul line in the Bulls’ season-opening loss to the Raptors gave the point total a welcome boost. He was considerably better against the Wizards, shooting over 50 percent from the field and finishing a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line. Given what he’s being asked to do as one of the Bulls’ young building blocks, Buzelis’ field-goal percentage may struggle. That said, he’s still someone who should be rostered in all fantasy leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 CJ McCollum finished with 17 points (7-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and one three-pointer against the Rockets on Saturday.
 McCollum has been a solid scorer for Atlanta so far this season, though he hasn’t contributed much value in other categories. 14 of his 17 points in this game came in the second half, but that wasn’t enough for them to get the win. McCollum should provide more assists than he has to this point, but in category leagues, the buckets are the only thing he’ll provide consistently.
